items.evidence: The overview's first section after the title is "## The bottom line", whose three paragraphs lead "**1. What FRUS answers directly.**", "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**" and "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**" in that order; "Scope" and "Decisions this needs from you" follow, and "## Findings" (1. Three standing tests...) comes only after them.

Every count or share names its set: "about twelve hundred documents in 73 volumes deal with whether Washington would recognize..."; "more than four in five of those that carry a source note came from the State Department's Central Decimal File"; "fewer than one document in twelve has a citation the index can resolve"; "The Mexican Estrada doctrine is named in 27 documents and the Venezuelan Betancourt doctrine in three... the other 84 documents the index returns for the name Tobar do not name the doctrine"; "'Department of State' appears in every one of the 74 volumes searched"; "1,227 documents in 73 volumes made up the working set"; "in roughly one working-set document in twelve"; "In the documents after 1948, communism comes up in about half and 'human rights' in about one in ten, against a few in a hundred for communism and none at all for human rights earlier"; "about one in three documents in the chosen chapters against about one in eight elsewhere in the same volumes"; "the nineteen documents this overview cites". No percent sign or bare percentage appears anywhere; the only figure without a set is the method's window "within 150 characters", a distance rather than a count.

All 25 citations of the 19 documents take the form series, year(s), part or volume where the edition has one, document number, link: "(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1895, Part I, Document 244, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1895p1/d244)", "(Foreign Relations, 1930, Volume I, Document 375, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1930v01/d375)", "(Foreign Relations, 1936, The American Republics, Volume V, Document 112, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1936v05/d112)", "(Foreign Relations, 1969–1976, Volume XXI, Document 348, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1969-76v21/d348)". The full series name appears in the first citation and the recognized short form "Foreign Relations" thereafter; the 1913 and 1917 annual editions carry no volume number because they have none. No document is cited by a bare id pair or by title alone. The collection holds the same 19 documents, each with a note and an excerpt matching the quotation.

The central absence is given as a search with terms, scope, counts and controls: "I searched the whole series for the region's own doctrines of recognition. The Mexican Estrada doctrine is named in 27 documents and the Venezuelan Betancourt doctrine in three. The Ecuadorian Tobar doctrine, the source of the Central American treaty rule, is named in one; the other 84 documents the index returns for the name Tobar do not name the doctrine. FRUS shows how Washington read these doctrines, not how the governments that framed them argued among themselves. The bundled indexes reach no foreign archive." and "The controls that make these absences meaningful: 'Department of State' appears in every one of the 74 volumes searched, and a nonsense string appears in none." Weaker: the other three absences (the 8 June 1948 circular "is cited... but not printed"; "no Central America volume after 1980"; the citation channel "has no entries before December 1910") are stated as catalogue and index-coverage facts rather than described searches, and the controls' 74 volumes are narrower than the whole series the doctrine search covered.

No SQL keyword, table or column name, or file path appears. Every frus identifier occurs only inside a history.state.gov URL (e.g. "https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1961-63v12/d421"), never as a bare pair; the sources are described in words ("a read-only copy of the FRUS Explorer search index covering all 553 published volumes, the TEI source files, and the reference data bundled with the app", "the index's word-root search", "(see the memo)"); the only codes are archival ones ("RG 59, entry A1 5763, NAID 1074073").

judge:r4.rankingReason:
r7: the fullest answer for the historian, 58 documents from 1865 to 1980 with every condition (elections, obligations, consultation, the treaty, the Axis, communism, civil liberties) counted against a named set by decade, four absences each given as a search with its terms, volumes, counts and a control, and the footnote-versus-document check made explicit; its only lapse is short-form repeat citations such as "(Document 849, link)".
r6: 43 documents built from the editors' own 62 recognition chapters, the sharpest "cannot get" section (four searches with terms, volumes, counts and the two controls inline, plus the finding that "by force" is not the documents' vocabulary) and the richest archival pointers (lot files with entry, NAID and access status, the POL 16 heading); one repeated 1936 citation lacks its link and the bullets cite without links, and it misses the March 1948 policy paper.
r5: 56 documents from 1877 to 1979, every citation in full form with a link even in the quotation bullets, the 1948 Policy Planning paper that lists the three factors in writing, and the 1979 "recognize nations, not governments" endpoint; part 2 runs long and partly on flagged inference, part 3 opens with an unmeasurable assertion before its searches, defers the volume list to the memo, and leaves the controls to the method section.
r4: the cleanest and shortest, 19 documents, every number based, uniform citations, controls stated inline, and a collection that mirrors it exactly with notes and excerpts; but it is the least complete of the four strong ones: it omits the 1923 adoption of Article II (frus1923v02/d345, cited by the other four) and the 1948 policy paper, so it tells the historian the three conditions may never have been "written down as policy" when FRUS prints the paper that lists them, and three of its four absences are asserted coverage facts rather than searches.
r3: a 38-document selection it calls "not a census", with recognition chapters found but left unread, an Afghanistan instruction brought in for a Latin American question, and many citations that give sender and date but no document number ("Acting Secretary Hill to Minister Hart, September 8, 1900") or neither; honest about its limits and sound on numbers and controls, but the thinnest answer.

score:r4.notes: All four files present. I re-derived the headline figures independently against the read-only copy and the bundled JSON: M0a; the M2a control from the log's verbatim 74-volume query (74|74|0|16905|0|61288|8290, IN list identical to scope_vols.txt); all eight FTS hit counts; 1,227 core docs in 73 volumes and the decade numerators from core.tsv; came-from (1,180 rows, era split, RG 59 1,047, 812.00 199) and pointed-at (155 rows in 97 docs, anchors 93/38/24, Carter NSA 27, LBJ NSF 6); earliest external_citations date 1910-12-06; 13 frus1981-88 volumes and 0 NEAR hits in frus1981-88v16's 88 docs; family cells for international obligations, treaty, Article 27 (13 strict/14 tolerant) and human rights; all 19 quotations as raw substrings; "usual tests" in frus1913/d894 and "Deptcircinstr June 8, 1948 Not printed" in frus1949v02/d439; every lot→NAID, series-fact year and status code, the Ecuador roll NAIDs, LBJ-NSF/JC-NSA NAIDs and the authority's lone "Central Decimal File 1910–1929" entry. Everything matched. The collection holds 19 documents and 19 excerpts equal to quotes.json, no Ed2, no duplicates. Flaws that fall under no item but an adjudicator should see: (a) the overview's "How this was done" says it worked from "the TEI source files" while memo §0 says "I did not open the TEI XML" (the memo is right; no TEI was read); (b) memo M8a says "Controls for these absences: M2a", but frus1981-88v16 is outside M2a's 74 volumes, so the stated control did not run over the volume whose zero it is offered for (the NEAR rule's 264 postwar rows are the real evidence the predicate returns rows); (c) the M7g library NAIDs and M7i roll NAIDs come from elided one-liners whose outputs were not saved (the log declares this; I verified the values); (d) the FTS table is joined on its content rowid, the schema's own link, never reported — scored obeyed under I2/I3 but noted in case the house rule reads stricter; (e) frus1977-80v09Ed2 is kept in the M3 denominator while the other two Ed2 volumes are excluded; this is correct, since only that Ed2 has no first edition in the copy, but the memo does not say why. One unmeasured qualitative change claim sits in the overview's Decisions section ("After 1948 the Department deliberately stopped using the word 'recognition'"); every counted change claim is bracketed in M4, so P2 stands.
